data.body:
Confirmed RCA before Phase 2

Mechanism: `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py:149-166` copies the full ordered `os.environ` into the returned `box` fixture. Pytest default/long traceback formatting renders function arguments through a 240-character `saferepr`; therefore ambient credentials early enough in that mapping are emitted verbatim in the ordinary failure header.

Discriminating proof used a fully sanitized `env -i`: with a synthetic sentinel inserted before PATH, the real existing failing node under default `pytest -q` printed the sentinel inside `box = {env: ...}`. Moving it after PATH hid it by repr truncation, explaining the first false-negative probe. Running the same failure with `--tb=short` removed the sentinel while child stdout/stderr and the assertion stayed unchanged, rejecting subprocess/autodeploy logging as the carrier. No real secret was logged.

Legitimacy: defect. The ticket AC requires a synthetic secret to be absent from failure output, and the security rubric forbids plaintext secrets in logs. A prior closed sibling `spodumene-stoned-arkshell` records the same broad-environment repr exposure.

Caller gate: only `_run` consumes `box[env]`; the harness needs PATH plus explicit test-owned variables (`DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX`, `HEALTH_TIMEOUT`). Sanitized reproductions prove it does not depend on ambient credentials.

Construct sweep found seven semantically equivalent returned-fixture mappings: test_autodeploy_materialize_probe.py, test_autodeploy_fetch_secrets.py, test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py, test_autodeploy_health_gate.py, test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py, test_observability_exit.py, and tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py. Each requires same-scope repair or a linked follow-up under Step 7.
